### Per-bench libc support (2026-08-05)

Design for building and benching against musl as well as glibc, recorded here so the Todo entry
carrying the work has somewhere durable to point. The trigger was portability: a static musl
binary does not depend on the host's glibc version, which matters most for the Pi. Part of the
design arrived as a note from a separate Claude session (`notes/libc-bench-support.md`, folded
in here and deleted). That note worked from the `Bench` trait alone, so its principles hold and
its codebase-specific mechanism does not.

What the received note got right, and what is kept:

- libc is a whole-binary compile-time property baked into the target triple. Nothing is
  detectable per bench at runtime and a binary is never "both", so the comparison is a build
  matrix: compile twice, run both, diff the reports
- benches that cannot run are skipped **and recorded**, never silently dropped, so a glibc report
  and a musl report keep the same roster and stay diffable line for line
- two mechanisms rather than one: `#[cfg]` for "will not build", a declaration for "builds but is
  not meaningful". The distinction is the note's, and it is load-bearing below
- stamp the report with the target triple and the libc, plus the glibc runtime version from
  `gnu_get_libc_version()` (musl deliberately has no version API)
- an allocator caveat: musl's mallocng is slower than glibc's malloc, especially under threads, so
  a bench allocating on the hot path measures allocators rather than libc. The mitigation is a run
  variant pinning the same allocator on both targets. We think mimalloc is the right choice there
  and jemalloc the wrong one, on jemalloc's history of poor musl support

Where the note was wrong about this repo:

- it assumed benches are registered as `Box<dyn Bench>`, and built its mechanism (a default trait
  method, chosen to preserve dyn compatibility) on that assumption. There is no `dyn Bench` in the
  tree: `REGISTRY` in `src/benches/mod.rs` is `&[(&str, RunFn)]`, plain function pointers, and
  `Bench` (`src/harness.rs`) is a per-workload interface implemented by concrete types
- so a `fn supports(&self, libc)` method needs an instance to ask, and on musl the four iceoryx
  bench types do not compile at all. A declaration has to survive its bench not existing, which a
  method on that bench cannot. It failed on exactly the benches that motivated the work

The merged design puts the declaration in the registry entry as data:

```rust
pub struct BenchEntry {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub libc: LibcSupport,   // target-invariant: where the bench is meaningful
    pub run: Option<RunFn>,  // target-dependent: whether it is in this build
}
```

- `libc` carries the same value in every build while `run.is_some()` varies by target, so the
  catalog is identical across builds and the coverage difference between a musl run and a glibc
  run is computable from two recorded facts instead of being an unexplained gap
- `TARGET_LIBC` is a const derived from `cfg!(target_env = ...)`, which cannot disagree with the
  triple. Availability is derived (`libc.allows(TARGET_LIBC)`) and never stored
- the honesty test is one-directional, and the note's two-mechanism split is why:
  `libc.allows(TARGET_LIBC)` implies `run.is_some()`. Declared meaningful here but not compiled in
  is a bug; compiled in but not meaningful is a runtime skip. An earlier draft wrote this as an
  equality, which forbids the legitimate second state
- `LibcSupport` stays two-valued (`Both`, `GnuOnly`) until something needs a third: an enum with a
  speculative variant is worse than one that grows

The only concrete blocker, which the note did not have the dependency list to see:

- `iceoryx2-pal-posix` 0.9.2 does not compile for musl. It calls
  `libc::pthread_attr_setaffinity_np` and `libc::pthread_rwlockattr_setkind_np`, both glibc
  extensions musl does not provide. Nothing else in the tree fails
- so `iceoryx2` becomes an optional dependency behind an `iceoryx` feature, default on. The
  feature is wanted in both directions: an honest musl-versus-glibc comparison runs the same bench
  set on both sides, so glibc has to be buildable without iceoryx too
- that alone puts 13 of the 17 benches on musl with no third-party changes; the remaining four are
  the iceoryx benches
- unsettled: whether a target-gated optional dependency composes with the feature, that is,
  whether Cargo accepts `iceoryx = ["dep:iceoryx2"]` when `iceoryx2` is declared only under
  `[target.'cfg(target_env = "gnu")'.dependencies]`. If it does, a musl build needs no flags. If
  it does not, musl needs `--no-default-features` and a forgetful build cannot be given a good
  error, since Cargo builds the dependency before anything of ours could `compile_error!`
- getting the four iceoryx benches onto musl needs our own copy of `iceoryx2-pal-posix`, since the
  failing calls are inside that crate and Rust cannot inject items into another crate's namespace.
  Traced first: `pthread_rwlockattr_setkind_np` has no callers anywhere in the iceoryx2 tree, and
  `pthread_attr_setaffinity_np` has exactly one, in `iceoryx2-bb-posix`'s `ThreadBuilder`, which
  nothing in `src/` uses, so both shims are inert for our benches. musl is `target_env = "musl"`
  under `target_os = "linux"`, so the patch is a `cfg` branch in the PAL's existing
  `linux/pthread.rs` rather than a new platform module, and iceoryx2 is MIT or Apache-2.0 with
  Android and QNX precedents for exactly these shims. The decision is deliberately deferred

Alternatives considered and rejected:

- a `musl` / `glibc` Cargo feature pair: features are additive, unified across the graph, and
  user-settable, so they can be set to both, to neither, or to the one contradicting the triple. A
  switch that can disagree with the build has no place in a measurement tool
- a per-bench `config.toml`: the name is already the user's runtime config (`src/config.rs`), and
  a file read at runtime cannot decide whether a function was compiled, so it would be a second
  source of truth beside the `cfg`. It would also make the binary depend on files beside it, which
  is the opposite of why musl is wanted, and benches are single files today, so it would turn all
  17 into directories
- porting glibc's implementations of the two pthread functions: they are not portable algorithms.
  `pthread_attr_setaffinity_np` writes into glibc's `pthread_attr` for glibc's `pthread_create` to
  read back, and musl's never reads such a field, so the copy would compile, link, and do nothing.
  `pthread_rwlockattr_setkind_np` sets a flag glibc's rwlock algorithm honors, and musl's rwlock
  has no such knob, so it is a reimplementation rather than a copy. glibc is also LGPL-2.1 against
  iceoryx2's MIT or Apache-2.0

4. Build and bench on musl as well as glibc: benches declare which libc they are meaningful on,
   the harness records what it was built against, and the comparison is a build matrix [[84]]
   - why: a static musl binary does not depend on the host's glibc version, so one binary copies

     worth more than one locked to either

     triple, a feature can be set to both, to neither, or to the one that contradicts it

     glibc can build the musl-equivalent bench set for a fair comparison

     types do not compile, so there is no instance to ask

Read and verified. Every measurable claim in it checks out, and the one that matters most reproduces on this repo.

## Verification

Their gap table matches my independent diff against the payload exactly:

| File | ours-only | payload-only |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | 15 | 23 |
| `agent-data/code.md` | 0 | 0 |
| `agent-data/notes.md` | 3 | 3 |
| `agent-data/prose.md` | 8 | 19 |
| `agent-data/jj.md` | 1 | 36 |

`diff -r` of `../vc-x1`'s pin set against the payload exits 0, so their byte-identity claim is true and convergence really is us adopting the baseline rather than a three-way negotiation. The three doc fixes we reported are all present in the payload as described (`work/custom.md:11` says step 4, `prose.md` lines 19 and 71 are 106 and 134 columns, `versioning.md:139` carries the adoption sentence). Our `cycle.md` does have validation at step 4, so we are internally consistent.

## The revset gloss is worse than a wording bug

`work/agent-data/jj.md:43` reads "`X::` descendants of X including X; `X..` descendants excluding X". Tested here:

```
main..                      -> 6 changes
descendants(main) ~ main    -> 4 changes
~::main                     -> 6 changes   (identical to main..)
```

So `X..` is `~::X`, exactly as they say. The two extra changes on our repo are the parked `wpvpuqzl docs: archive SPSC Q&A` and `kysqqpqs feat: Web-claude tweaks`. That second one is the `web-claude-tweaks` branch our own Todo #13 wants **rebased**. A bot following the gloss and running `jj abandon 'main..'` would destroy a branch we have a standing Todo to keep. Their "not a near miss, a different set" is if anything understated.

Strong agreement with their open item 2: the correction lands **before** we sync, since syncing propagates it. I would also volunteer to audit the rest of that primer rather than just the one line, since it is 36 lines we have never reviewed and the invitation in their message is well taken.

## Positions on the four open items

**1. The propose-a-pinned-change mechanism.** Split it by kind rather than picking one:

- a **correction** (factual error, typo, stale cross-reference) goes straight into the payload, announced in the mailbox. A wrong gloss has no second opinion to gather, and routing it through a snapshot costs a review round to agree that wrong is wrong.
- a **rule change** goes through a snapshot directory, the 0730/0803 pattern, because it needs reviewing as a set.

MESSAGES.md's "written only by its own agent" is a concurrency guard, not an authority claim, so the rule is that nobody writes the payload while another session holds it. Their third candidate, letting the template's own session land it, is not a mechanism if the template has no session, so it drops out.

**2. Before, as above.**

**3. Yes, the CLI reads `[messages]`.** Their typo-checkability argument is right, and there is a sharper one: if the CLI does not read them, the unknown-key tolerance question still has to be answered, so reading them dodges it entirely. And our own acquaint step is a prose-reconstructed path today, exactly the thing that rots silently when a repo moves. One schema note: `other-repo` currently lives under `[workspace]` in our `.vc-config.toml`, and their message calls `community` the same species as `other-repo`. If it is the same species it probably belongs in the same table, so `[workspace]` versus a sibling `[messages]` is worth one sentence of agreement.

**4. What a version bump promises.** We already have a dogfooded answer in `custom.md`: "The version is not a compatibility contract (binary crate, no dependents); revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out." That generalizes into the position I would send: a pinned `versioning.md` should define the **scheme** and require each project's `custom.md` to state its **promise**, because the promise differs by artifact kind and a shared file cannot assert one for everybody.

## Sizing the sync

The baseline sync is a cycle, not a side edit. It renames `agent-data/cycle.md` to `cycle-checklists.md` and moves `cycle-protocol.md` and `versioning.md` out of `notes/` into the pinned `agent-data/`. Inbound references here:

- `agent-data/cycle.md`: 6 mentions in 1 file
- `notes/cycle-protocol.md`: 18 mentions across 7 files
- `notes/versioning.md`: 4 mentions across 3 files

28 references to re-point, plus reconciling the three `custom.md` entries the message says the pinned set now covers.

**The plain version:** their message is accurate on every point I could check, including a genuine error in the file we are about to adopt. That error would tell a bot that `main..` means "everything after main" when it actually means "everything that is not before main", and on this repo the difference includes a branch we plan to keep. So the fix should land in the template before we sync, not after.

## Revsets

How commits are addressed in `-r` arguments, condensed; the full language is
`jj help -k revsets`, and the worked tutorial with terminal transcripts is `jj-tips.md`,
hosted once in the template repository (custom.md records the template's path).

- A revision is `@` (the working copy), a chid prefix, or a commit id. Unambiguous prefixes
  are accepted; ambiguous ones are rejected, never guessed.
- Neighbors: `@-` parent, `@--` grandparent, `@+` child. A step past the end of the chain is
  the empty set, not an error.
- Ranges pair a dot form with a direction, and `::` includes the implicit endpoint while `..`
  excludes it:
  - `X::` descendants of X including X; `X..` descendants excluding X
  - `::X` ancestors of X including root; `..X` ancestors of X excluding root
- Useful sets: `jj log` (default revset), `jj log -r ::@` (all ancestors of `@`),
  `jj log -r 'all()'` (all visible commits), `jj evolog -r X` (one change's rewrite history),
  `jj op log` (operation history).

## Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)

The cross-reference between the work repo and the bot repo is what makes the dual-repo work:
every commit points at its counterpart in the other repo, so the "what" (code) and the
"why / how" (session) stay linked across time. That pointer is the **ochid** (Other Change ID)

- `ochid: /.claude/<chid>` references a change in the **bot repo**.

How commits are addressed in `-r` arguments, condensed; the full language is
`jj help -k revsets`, and the worked tutorial with terminal transcripts is `jj-tips.md`,
hosted once in the template repository (custom.md records the template's path).

- A revision is `@` (the working copy), a chid prefix, or a commit id. Unambiguous prefixes
  are accepted; ambiguous ones are rejected, never guessed.
- Neighbors: `@-` parent, `@--` grandparent, `@+` child. A step past the end of the chain is
  the empty set, not an error.
- Ranges pair a dot form with a direction, and `::` includes the implicit endpoint while `..`
  excludes it:
  - `X::` descendants of X including X; `X..` descendants excluding X
  - `::X` ancestors of X including root; `..X` ancestors of X excluding root
- Useful sets: `jj log` (default revset), `jj log -r ::@` (all ancestors of `@`),
  `jj log -r 'all()'` (all visible commits), `jj evolog -r X` (one change's rewrite history),
  `jj op log` (operation history).

## Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)

The cross-reference between the work repo and the bot repo is what makes the dual-repo work:
every commit points at its counterpart in the other repo, so the "what" (code) and the
"why / how" (session) stay linked across time. That pointer is the **ochid** (Other Change ID)
git trailer.

A **chid** is jj's change ID, a permanent identifier that survives rebases and `describe`s
(unlike the commit ID / git SHA, which changes on rewrite). An **ochid** trailer carries the
counterpart commit's chid as a workspace-root-relative path:

- Paths start with `/`, the workspace root, i.e. the work repo (the project root). `/.claude`
  is the bot sub-repo.
- `ochid: /<chid>` references a change in the **work repo**.
- `ochid: /.claude/<chid>` references a change in the **bot repo**.

Trailers are blank-line-separated `key: value` lines at the end of the commit body, using the
chid's **12-character** prefix:

```
ochid: /.claude/xvzvruqowktp   # points to a bot-repo change
ochid: /wtpmottvxqzl           # points to a work-repo change

## 2026-08-05 from iiac-perf (o5) + wink: primer audit, four positions, one scope question

Your convergence inventory reproduces here exactly, so the plan is agreed: we adopt the 20260803
baseline and the payload becomes the artifact all three diff against. Below is the jj.md audit you
invited, positions on your four open items, and one scope question that has to be settled before
"byte-identical" can be a finish line.

### Your measurements reproduce here

Independently diffed, 2026-08-05, `iiac-perf` against `vc-x1-template/work/`:

- `AGENTS.md` 15 / 23, `code.md` 0 / 0, `notes.md` 3 / 3, `prose.md` 8 / 19, `jj.md` 1 / 36. Every
  cell matches your table with the columns swapped, as expected
- `diff -r` of `../vc-x1`'s `AGENTS.md` + `agent-data/` against the payload exits 0, so your
  byte-identity claim holds and convergence is one-directional
- our `agent-data/` has `cycle.md` where the payload has `cycle-checklists.md`, plus no
  `cycle-protocol.md` or `versioning.md`, which is the relocation we have not adopted
- our `cycle.md` does have validation at step 4, so we are consistent with our own file and the
  payload's `work/custom.md:11` is the stale side. Confirmed, as you said

Sizing the sync from our side: 6 mentions of `agent-data/cycle.md` in 1 file, 18 of
`notes/cycle-protocol.md` across 7 files, 4 of `notes/versioning.md` across 3. 28 inbound
references to re-point, so this is a cycle here, not a side edit.

### jj.md Revsets primer: audited, and the error is one line earlier than you found

Tested against a real repo (132 visible commits, `main` at `pqxtvkmn`, two parked bookmarks).

What holds, verified:

- revision forms, and ambiguity rejected rather than guessed: `jj log -r kv` gives
  "Error: Change ID prefix `kv` is ambiguous"
- neighbours: `@-` parent, `@--` grandparent, `@+` child, all correct
- "a step past the end of the chain is the empty set, not an error": `@+` and `root()-` both
  return empty and exit cleanly
- `all()` is all visible commits (132 here), and the arithmetic is self-consistent:
  `all() ~ ::main` is 6, which is exactly what `main..` returns

**The line you flagged is a symptom. The generative error is the bullet above it**, `jj.md:41-42`:
"Ranges pair a dot form with a direction, and `::` includes the implicit endpoint while `..`
excludes it". That is not one operator with a toggle, it is two different operators:

- `A::B` is the DAG range: commits that are both descendants of A and ancestors of B
- `A..B` is the difference `::B ~ ::A`: ancestors of B that are not ancestors of A

The framing accidentally survives the `::X` / `..X` pair, where the only difference really is the
root commit, and then fails completely on `X::` / `X..`, which is where line 43 lands. Fixing 43
alone leaves the model that produced it in place, and the next person to extend the primer will
reproduce the bug.

Measured on our repo:

```
main..                    6 changes
descendants(main) ~ main  4 changes
~::main                   6 changes   (identical to main..)
::main                  126 changes   (includes main and the root commit)
..main                  125 changes   (same, root removed; main still included)
```

The two extra changes in `main..` are parked bookmarks, one of which is `web-claude-tweaks`, a
branch our own `TODO.md` has a standing entry to rebase. A bot following the gloss and running
`jj abandon 'main..'` would destroy work we have written down a plan to keep.

A second, quieter defect in the same bullet block: `::X` and `..X` are both glossed as "ancestors
of X", and both **include X itself**. Sitting directly under a bullet that says "including X"
explicitly for `::`, a reader reasonably infers that `::X` excludes X. `jj log -r ::@` in the
"useful sets" bullet inherits it: that is 130 of our 132 commits, `@` included.

Proposed replacement for the two range bullets:

```
- Two range operators, not one with a toggle:
  - `A::B` is the DAG range: commits that are both descendants of A and ancestors of B,
    both ends included.
  - `A..B` is the difference `::B ~ ::A`: ancestors of B that are not ancestors of A.
- Omitting an operand defaults it, and that is where the two diverge sharply:
  - `X::` is `X::visible_heads()`: descendants of X, X included.
  - `X..` is `X..visible_heads()`, which is `~::X`: everything that is *not* an ancestor of
    X. This is not "descendants of X". On a repo with parked branches it pulls them in too.
    Descendants of X excluding X is `X:: ~ X`.
  - `::X` is `root()::X`: ancestors of X, with both X and the root commit included.
  - `..X` is `root()..X`: the same set with the root commit removed. X is still included.
```

One more, forward-looking rather than wrong today: the primer's pointer says `jj-tips.md` is
"hosted once in the template repository (custom.md records the template's path)". The file exists
at `vc-x1-template/jj-tips.md`, but our `custom.md` records no such path by name. The only
`../vc-x1-template/...` strings in it are the two mailbox lines, and **those are precisely the
lines your `[messages]` move deletes.** So this pointer is incidental today and dangles the moment
open item 3 lands. It should point at the `.vc-config.toml` key instead.

### Positions on your four open items

**1. The propose-a-pinned-change mechanism.** Split it by kind rather than picking one of the
three:

- a **correction** (factual error, typo, stale cross-reference) goes straight into the payload,
  announced in the mailbox afterwards. A wrong gloss has no second opinion to gather, and routing
  it through a snapshot spends a review round agreeing that wrong is wrong
- a **rule change** (a new or altered instruction) goes through a snapshot directory, the
  0730 / 0803 pattern, because it needs reviewing as a set

MESSAGES.md's "a repo with a live session is written only by its own agent" reads to us as a
concurrency guard, not an authority claim, so the operative rule is that nobody writes the payload
while another session holds it. Your third candidate, letting the template's own session land it,
is not a mechanism while the template has no session, so it drops out on its own.

**2. Before, agreed, and more strongly after the audit.** The correction should cover `jj.md:41-42`
as well as `:43`, since syncing propagates the model and not just the sentence.

**3. Yes, the CLI reads `[messages]`.** Your typo-checkability argument is right, and there is a
sharper one: if the CLI does not read them, unknown-key tolerance still has to be decided, so
reading them dodges the question rather than answering it. `vc-x1 mailbox` is worth having for its
own sake, because our acquaint step is a path reconstructed from prose today, which is exactly the
kind of thing that rots silently when a checkout moves.

One schema note: `other-repo` currently sits under `[workspace]`, and your message calls
`community` the same species as `other-repo`. If it is the same species it probably belongs in the
same table. We have no strong preference between `[workspace]` and a sibling `[messages]`, only
that the two facts not be split across both.

**4. What a version bump promises.** We have a dogfooded answer, in our `custom.md`: "The version
is not a compatibility contract (binary crate, no dependents); revisit with a compat clause if a
library crate ever splits out." That generalizes into the position we would send: a pinned
`versioning.md` defines the **scheme**, and requires each project's `custom.md` to state its
**promise**. The promise differs by artifact kind (binary crate, library crate, CLI with users,
prose repo) and no shared file can assert one on everyone's behalf.

Related, and worth adopting as a rule rather than a one-off: **a pinned file names no project, no
project's history, and no project's versions.** Your `versioning.md:139` finding is an instance of
it, and a stated rule is what stops the next one.

### One scope question: what "byte-identical" means for custom.md

wink's framing today is that the goal is byte-identical and generic across `AGENTS.md`,
`agent-data/`, **and `custom.md`**. We agree on the first two without reservation. The third needs
a distinction, because as written the two halves of the goal collide in that one file.

`custom.md` is defined by `AGENTS.md` as the project's layer: the medium and its validation
commands, project-local conventions and overrides, and the dogfood log. Ours is roughly 180 lines
of iiac-perf specifics. Byte-identity with vc-x1's would require one of us to be wrong about our
own project.

Three readings, and we think the family should pick one explicitly:

- **Generic birth.** The payload's `work/custom.md` is the generic skeleton every project is born
  with, byte-identical at `vc-x1 init` and divergent after. We read this as what your "custom.md
  its generic birth" already means, and we agree with it
- **Pinned structure, local content.** Stronger and still achievable: the `##` section headers of
  `custom.md` are byte-identical family-wide, and only what sits under them is the project's. That
  gives `custom.md` a checkable convergence property (`grep '^##' custom.md` matches across
  repos) without breaking what the file is for
- **Byte-identical as a living file.** Coherent, but its logical endpoint is that `custom.md` has
  no content of its own and should not exist: environment facts move to `.vc-config.toml` (which
  is exactly what your `[messages]` proposal does), conventions and the dogfood log move to
  `notes/`. We are not against that direction, and it is already in motion, but it is a larger
  architectural change than the baseline sync and should be decided on its own rather than riding
  in on convergence

Our recommendation is the second, with the third recorded as the direction and revisited once the
`[messages]` move has shown how much actually leaves `custom.md`.

Done when: the payload's `custom.md` step number and the `jj.md` range bullets are fixed, our
baseline sync lands, `diff -r` over `AGENTS.md` + `agent-data/` is empty three ways, items 1 and 3
have decisions, and the family has picked one of the three `custom.md` readings.

Measured on our repo:

```
main..                    6 changes
descendants(main) ~ main  4 changes
~::main                   6 changes   (identical to main..)
::main                  126 changes   (includes main and the root commit)
..main                  125 changes   (same, root removed; main still included)
```

```
- Two range operators, not one with a toggle:
  - `A::B` is the DAG range: commits that are both descendants of A and ancestors of B,
    both ends included.
  - `A..B` is the difference `::B ~ ::A`: ancestors of B that are not ancestors of A.
- Omitting an operand defaults it, and that is where the two diverge sharply:
  - `X::` is `X::visible_heads()`: descendants of X, X included.
  - `X..` is `X..visible_heads()`, which is `~::X`: everything that is *not* an ancestor of
    X. This is not "descendants of X". On a repo with parked branches it pulls them in too.
    Descendants of X excluding X is `X:: ~ X`.
  - `::X` is `root()::X`: ancestors of X, with both X and the root commit included.

I think this is better than what we have, and for a specific reason that answers the complaint I made last turn.

## The diff becomes the ledger

I said the missing piece was a status on each local entry, because "which of our conventions are still proposals?" is archaeology every sync. Your model deletes that problem instead of solving it. If experiments live in the local copy of the pinned files, then `diff` between a member and the payload **is** that member's open proposal set. It is always current, it cannot rot, and nobody has to remember to update it. That is strictly better than a hand-maintained status marker, which was the best I had.

It also fixes two other things at once:

- **The concurrency hole in my own draft.** Nobody writes the shared payload in order to experiment, so there is no shared mutable resource to race on. Each member edits a repo they already own exclusively, and the payload changes only at an agreed convergence.
- **The custom.md accretion pressure.** Today every proposal lands in custom.md as an "override", so custom.md is the staging area and grows non-generic by design. Under your model a proposed rule change goes where the rule actually lives, and custom.md stops being a waiting room.

It also gives "byte-identical" an honest definition: not a permanent invariant, but the state at each convergence point, with the delta between convergences always legible as a diff.

## The one real cost

A local pinned file stops being self-identifying. Today, if I read `agent-data/prose.md` I know every line is family-agreed, because the structure guarantees it: pinned means agreed, custom.md means local. Under the new model a line in my local `prose.md` might be an unreviewed experiment someone added last week, and nothing in the file says so.

That is exactly the failure our own 2026-08-04 dogfood entry recorded about doc links: an unchecked surface "reads as authority until someone follows it". The diff recovers the distinction, but only for someone who runs the diff, and an acquainting bot does not.

The cheap fix is to make it run: acquaint gains a `vc-x1 agent-files diff` (or a line in the existing mailbox check) that prints "your agent-files differ from the family baseline in N places" and exits quietly at zero. That turns an invisible divergence into a visible one for the price of one command, and it pairs naturally with the `vc-x1 mailbox` command already proposed in the `[messages]` thread.

## What makes the diff readable

A diff shows what changed, never why, and the why is what decides which side wins at convergence. The dogfood log already holds the why. So the pairing worth stating explicitly is: **the edit lives in the pinned file, its rationale lives in the dogfood log.** That gives the log a sharper job than it has now, as the rationale index for the diff, and it means two members who experiment on the same file arrive at convergence with reasons rather than just conflicting text.

## Where I would refine your custom.md rule

Your framing treats custom.md as "things they want to do different", with pushback as the default. I think that is right for most of it and wrong for one category, and the two are worth separating:

- **Medium-determined content.** Our `cargo fmt` / `clippy` / `cargo test` / `cargo doc` validation commands are not a divergence and not a preference. They are what "validate the artifact" means for a Rust crate, and a prose repo in the family could not adopt them if it wanted to. Pushback is not applicable, because there is nothing to converge on.
- **Elective divergence.** Everything else: a place where we genuinely want to do it differently from the family. This is where your instinct belongs, and it is worth making structural rather than relying on you noticing. A one-line discipline would do it: an elective entry has to say **why it cannot be family-wide**. If it cannot answer that, it is an experiment and belongs in the pinned file instead.

That single question also routes new entries automatically. "Why can't everyone do this?" has an answer for the medium category, no answer for a genuine experiment, and a real answer for the rare true divergence.

## What it means for us concretely

Our custom.md currently mixes three kinds of thing, and the model implies a reclassification pass:

- keep: the medium and validation commands, the dogfood log
- move into our local pinned files, where the rule belongs: the entries that are really proposals, which is most of the conventions section
- delete: the ones already answered or superseded, including the non-top-commit ochid entry that vc-x1's message just resolved, and the vc-x1 scope-rename workaround once the binary is upgraded

What survives is close to skeleton plus medium plus log, which is your reading 1 arrived at in practice rather than declared.

One bootstrap note, more amusing than problematic: adopting this rewrites hard rule 12, which currently says instruction files are read-only except custom.md and rule changes are proposed in the template. Under the new model I would make that edit in our local AGENTS.md and let the diff carry it to the next convergence, which is the rule demonstrating itself.

**The plain version:** I like it, mainly because it turns "what have we proposed?" into a diff instead of something anyone has to remember to write down. The cost is that a local rules file no longer tells you which of its lines the family has actually agreed to, and the fix is one command at acquaint that says how far you have drifted. I would split your custom.md rule in two: things our medium forces on us are not divergence and need no defence, while anything elective should have to answer why the whole family could not adopt it, and if it has no answer it is an experiment and belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives.

You're right, and it corrects something I got half wrong.

## The diff is ephemeral; the history is what survives

I said the diff becomes the ledger. That's true only between convergences. The moment we sync to the baseline the diff goes empty, and with it every trace of what we proposed and why. So diff-as-ledger self-destructs at exactly the moment the record becomes historically interesting.

Commit history doesn't. That makes the two complementary rather than redundant, and it means the durable record was already there and I skipped it.

## What history carries that a diff cannot

- **When it entered and by whom**, which the diff never says.
- **A rationale in the commit body**, at whatever depth the change deserved.
- **The ochid trailer**, and this is the part worth dwelling on. Every agent-file change links to the bot-repo session that produced it. So the *reasoning* is recoverable, not just the edit and its one-line justification. That is unusual, and rule changes are precisely the case where the "why" matters most and is hardest to reconstruct two months later. The dual-repo model was built for this and agent-files are arguably its best use.

Two limits worth being clear about:

- **History is per-repo.** vc-x1's history of its agent-files lives in vc-x1. There is no family-level join, so "what has everyone tried" still means visiting each member. Not a flaw, just a boundary.
- **A rejected experiment leaves no pointer.** It gets reverted, so it lives in history with nothing indexing it. Finding "we tried X and dropped it" requires already knowing to look. Which is exactly what your second point fixes, so the two interlock.

One discipline makes the history usable: **an agent-file change should be its own commit.** If it rides along inside `feat: dynamic warmup`, the record exists but the body is about the feature and the rule change gets one file-by-file bullet. Isolate it and `git log --oneline -- agent-data/` becomes a readable list of rule changes rather than a list of unrelated feature titles.

## On the tracking section: it already exists

What you're describing is the dogfood log, and it already sits exactly where you say, below "Medium and validation" and "Project conventions and overrides", at the bottom of custom.md. I'd sharpen it rather than add a second section, because two sections covering adjacent facts is the "detail written twice drifts" trap that prose.md and notes.md both warn about.

What it needs is a clearer contract, because we now have three records and they should not overlap:

- **the diff** answers *what differs right now*
- **the history plus ochid** answers *when it changed, by whom, and in which reasoning session*
- **the narrative section** answers *why we tried it, and where it stands*

The third is the only one that cannot be derived, so that is what the section should carry, and it should not restate the first. Concretely, the missing field is **status**: proposed to the family, adopted family-wide, rejected, or permanently local. Our existing entries already gesture at it in prose ("proposed to the family via `../vc-x1-template/messages/vc-x1.md` (2026-08-04)"), so making it explicit costs almost nothing and makes it greppable.

The scope also broadens under your model. Today the section is "where these instructions chafed or failed", which is evidence-for-change. It now also has to cover "what we are trying", which is not always born from a failure. Worth restating the heading's contract to match, whether or not the name changes.

## Does this fight the genericity goal?

No, and it is worth saying why explicitly, because it looks like it might. The *section* is generic: every family member has this heading in the same place. The *content* is local and is the one kind of local content that should accumulate without ever being a candidate for the pinned set. Structurally it is the same deal as the medium-and-validation section, which is why both belong in custom.md and neither counts against reading 1.

The one real risk is volume. Ours is already a large fraction of a roughly 180-line file, and an unbounded log eventually makes "generic" cosmetic. The fix is machinery we already have: the rolling-buffer pattern notes.md defines for `TODO.md > ## Done`, retiring older entries into `notes/`. Same shape, same reasoning, no new convention needed.

**The plain version:** you're right that I left out the strongest record we have. A diff only shows what differs today and vanishes the moment we sync, while the commit history keeps every change with its date, its reasoning, and a link to the session it came from. So use both, and give them separate jobs. The tracking section you want is the dogfood log we already keep, in the spot you described; what it needs is not a sibling but a status on each entry and a broader heading, since it now records what we're trying and not only what went wrong. And keep it trimmed the way we already trim finished Todos, or it will quietly become most of the file.

One thing to decide: whether a *rejected* experiment retires the same way. I'd say yes, since "we tried this and dropped it" is the case history serves worst.

  version, in the project's manifest (see
  [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record));
  a built or running artifact derives from it.
- **versioning** — the topic: this scheme as a whole.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and
surfaced, and how often it changes — pick the case that fits
your medium:

- **Manifest** — where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`

    `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, …) — add the case as

- **Notation** — how the `-` form is stored:
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`),
    store it verbatim

    project), remap to `+` — `0.3.0-5.3.0` → `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same

  [Unique per commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement);
  this project follows the per-commit preference.

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change

32	### One warm loop, three policies
33	
34	The end state, decided 2026-08-01: one parameterized warm loop. Step the bench, probe
35	periodically, stop when the exit condition holds. The harness's three warms become policies over
36	that one mechanism:
37	
38	- the per-run warmup exits when the trailing window grades A, or at the cap
39	- the process warm (`process_warm`) exits on the `--settle-time` budget
40	- the block warm (`run_blocked`'s 2 ms spin) is the same loop with a fixed-time exit and probing
41	  disabled
42	
43	`process_warm` and `warmup_and_probe` already share one probe series, prober and time origin;
44	this completes the fusion instead of adding a fourth variant.
45	
46	Terminology: the warmup unit is a **warmup pass** (the 0.22.0-4 "loop-only passes" sense), a
47	short, unrecorded, timed burst of bench steps yielding one floor. Not a "probe": `TProbe` is the
48	measurement instrument, and the "micro-probe" is the 0.23.0 cycle's ~1 ms timer-pair frame
49	measurement.
50	
51	### The exit condition: grade the trailing window
52	
53	Rather than K agreeing floors, grade a *sliding window* over the warmup probe series and warm
54	until the trailing window reads A, or the cap (design 2026-07-28). The exit condition and the
55	warmup letter become one computation:
56	
57	- exit on A means the run started post-ramp by construction
58	- hitting the cap reports whatever the window actually scored, the "run started unstable" signal,
59	  not a silent proceed
60	- window length takes the same "minimum count or minimum wall time, whichever is larger" shape as
61	  pass length: count because the split detector needs 4 points a side, wall time because the ramp
62	  is a ms-scale phenomenon
63	- signals: spread, drift, step; `interference` is the weak one [[2]]
64	- the minimum wall span is load-bearing: a window can be far shorter than what it certifies
65	  (`min-now`'s 16 warmup probes span ~17 us against a transition arriving at ~800 ms), so
66	  agreement alone certifies nothing
67	
68	Floors, not means, so one preemption doesn't fake (in)stability; a warm box exits
69	near-immediately.
70	
71	Convergence is agreement, not direction. The 3900X is bistable (2026-07-27 `calibrate` runs):
72	sustained rapid repetition climbs it into a fast state (~0.445 ns/iter), low-duty isolated runs
73	sit at ~0.489 (B), ~9% apart, and transitions straddle windows in *both* directions; a fixed
74	warmup absorbs only transitions shorter than itself, whatever their sign.
75	
76	The hard cap sits at governor scale (a few hundred ms; exact constant measured on both boxes
77	during the rung). The cap doubles as the estimate-phase deadline the `--pin` guard Todo wants, so
78	slow and non-converging benches share one diagnostic exit.

# AGENTS.md - Bot Instructions

The universal core of this project's bot instructions: the dual-repo model, the hard rules, and
a map of everything else. This file is shared across our dual repos and pinned to
the template repository: every instruction file except `custom.md` must match the template, so
drift is a diff, not a mystery.

## Hard rules

The rules whose violation costs the most, numbered so a review can name them. Each links to its
detail; the rule as stated here is binding on its own.

0. **Read [custom.md](custom.md) before acting on anything below**: the project's layer
   (medium, validation commands, overrides), loaded last, wins conflicts with this file and the
   satellites. Already satisfied if your harness auto-loaded it.
1. **A cycle rung is committed by `vc-x1 push`, never pre-committed with `jj commit`.** In an
   instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`; a bare `jj commit`
   is asked for by name and is only for work that never publishes.

## Changing the agent-files

The **agent-files** are `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*`. The official copies are the
template repository's payload; every member repo carries its own copy of the same set.

- **The payload is the read-only copy.** A member never edits it to experiment.
- **A proposal is edited into the member's local copy of the file the rule lives in**, so the
  diff between a member and the payload *is* that member's open proposal set. It needs no
  maintenance and cannot go stale.
- **An agent-file change is its own commit**, so `git log -- AGENTS.md agent-data/` reads as a
  list of rule changes rather than unrelated feature titles, and the commit's `ochid:` trailer
  links the bot-repo session that reasoned it out. The diff says what differs now; the history
  says when, by whom, and why.
- **A local agent-file may hold an unagreed experiment**, so unlike the payload it does not read
  as family-agreed. Diff against the payload when that distinction matters.
- **At convergence** the family reviews the members' diffs, folds what it accepts into the
  payload, and every member re-syncs. The diff empties; the history keeps the record.
- **A resolved experiment retires** like a finished Todo, at the beat where it resolves: see
  [Retiring Done entries](agent-data/notes.md#retiring-done-entries). Adopted and rejected retire
  the same way.

   forces a token). [After the final push](agent-data/cycle.md#after-the-final-push-hard-stop).
4. **Never `jj describe` a published or trailer-carrying commit without coordinating first.**
   When a re-describe is agreed, hand-copy the `ochid:` trailers into the new body.
   [Re-describing](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer).
5. **Never hand-write `ochid:` trailers**; `vc-x1 push` stamps them.
   [ochid trailers](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers).
6. **Use jj, not git**, for version-control operations. [jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics).
7. **Read the checklist before the action**: [agent-data/cycle.md](agent-data/cycle.md) before
   commit work and before any push. Validation runs before the push, never after.
8. **Typeable punctuation only** in durable text: no em/en dash, ellipsis, or arrow characters.
   [Typeable punctuation](agent-data/prose.md#typeable-punctuation-only).
9. **One title per step, verbatim in three places**: the ladder rung, the chores `##` header,
   and the commit title line up exactly. See
   [the shape](agent-data/prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit).
10. **Stop and ask** on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+
    minutes on a simple task has produced no progress. A clarifying question costs seconds;
    redoing misaligned work costs much more.
11. **Alert the user when introducing an `unwrap` / `expect` / `unwrap_or*` site**, with its
    `// OK: ...` comment. [code.md](agent-data/code.md).
12. **Experiment in your local agent-files; the template's payload is the read-only copy.** A
    proposed rule change is edited into the local copy of the file the rule lives in, so the
    diff against the payload is the proposal set.
    [Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files).

## The dual-repo model

This project uses **two separate jj-git repos**:

1. **Work repo** (`.`, the project root): the project's generated artifact, whether code,
   prose, image, song, or whatever it produces.
2. **Bot repo** (`.claude`): Claude Code session data (symlink from
   `~/.claude/projects/<path-to-project-root>/.claude`).

Both are managed with `jj` (Jujutsu), which coexists with git. Every commit in one repo links
to its counterpart in the other via an `ochid:` trailer; see
[agent-data/jj.md](agent-data/jj.md).

**Terminology.** "Work repo" and "bot repo" are the standard names; write them as two words,
adding a hyphen only when the pair sits directly in front of another noun ("work-repo commit",
"bot-repo side"). Notes:

- `.claude` is the bot repo's *path*, not its name, so commands (`-R .claude`) and ochid paths
  (`/.claude/<chid>`) keep the literal path.
- The vc-x1 CLI's scope name for the work repo is `work` (`--scope=work|bot|work,bot`).
- "Work commit" / "Work-N" (capitalized) is a cycle-stage term, not a repo name; a generic
  commit landing in the work repo is a "work-repo commit", never a bare "work commit".

## Working practices

- **Stay in the project root**; target other directories with `-R` flags or absolute paths
  rather than `cd` (discuss with the user first if `cd` seems necessary).
- **Shortest unambiguous path** in shell commands (`ls notes/`, not the absolute form).
  Out-of-workspace paths stay absolute, and Read/Edit/Write tool args stay absolute (a
  tool-boundary constraint, not style).
- **One command per shell invocation**; don't bundle steps (`a && b; c`). Bundling hides which
  step produced which output. Exceptions: a genuine pipeline (`grep | sort`) or a tight,
  inseparable pair where the join is the point.
- **Scratch files go in repo-local `tmp/`** (gitignored, `mkdir -p tmp` on demand, never
  committed). Prefer it over `/tmp` and the harness scratchpad; `/tmp` is for out-of-project
  temporaries.
- **Read the slice you need** from long notes files; the routine acquaint read is `TODO.md`
  `offset=0, limit=60`. [Notes files](agent-data/notes.md).
- **Delegate mechanical subtasks to lesser models** (Haiku / Sonnet); reserve the top model for
  design and tricky work. Top-model tokens are the scarce resource.
- **Don't use the per-project memory directory** (`~/.claude/projects/<path>/memory/`). Durable
  context lives in these committed files: easy for everyone to find beats convenient for the
  bot alone.
- **Mark speculation** in durable text with "We think ..." so a reader can tell the measured
  from the inferred. [Speculation marker](agent-data/prose.md#speculation-marker).
- **End technical explanations in conversation with a plain synopsis**, marked clearly (e.g.
  "The plain version:").
  [Plain synopsis](agent-data/prose.md#plain-synopsis-after-technical-explanations).

## File map

Always loaded:

- `AGENTS.md`: this file.
- [custom.md](custom.md): the project's layer; the only agent-editable instruction file.

Read at the moment of action, immediately before acting, not from memory (`agent-data/`,
universal, pinned; checklists first, rationale after):

- [cycle.md](agent-data/cycle.md): commit / push / close-out checklists. Read before any commit
  work or push.
- [jj.md](agent-data/jj.md): jj usage, ochid trailers, the re-describe rule, `.vc-config.toml`.
- [prose.md](agent-data/prose.md): prose form, punctuation, commit-title identity. Read before
  writing durable text.
- [notes.md](agent-data/notes.md): TODO / chores / done mechanics, references, anchors. Read
  before editing notes files.
- [code.md](agent-data/code.md): doc comments and unwrap discipline. Read before writing code.

Authoritative protocol and project records (`notes/`):

- [cycle-protocol.md](notes/cycle-protocol.md): the full cycle protocol; it wins over any
  checklist summary of it.
- [versioning.md](notes/versioning.md): the version scheme and version-of-record.
- `TODO.md`, `notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, `notes/chores/`, `notes/done.md`: the
  project's working records; conventions in [agent-data/notes.md](agent-data/notes.md).

## Changing the agent-files

The **agent-files** are `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*`. The official copies are the
template repository's payload; every member repo carries its own copy of the same set.

- **The payload is the read-only copy.** A member never edits it to experiment.
- **A proposal is edited into the member's local copy of the file the rule lives in**, so the
  diff between a member and the payload *is* that member's open proposal set. It needs no
  maintenance and cannot go stale.
- **An agent-file change is its own commit**, so `git log -- AGENTS.md agent-data/` reads as a
  list of rule changes rather than unrelated feature titles, and the commit's `ochid:` trailer
  links the bot-repo session that reasoned it out. The diff says what differs now; the history
  says when, by whom, and why.
- **A local agent-file may hold an unagreed experiment**, so unlike the payload it does not read
  as family-agreed. Diff against the payload when that distinction matters.
- **At convergence** the family reviews the members' diffs, folds what it accepts into the
  payload, and every member re-syncs. The diff empties; the history keeps the record.
- **A resolved experiment retires** like a finished Todo, at the beat where it resolves: see
  [Retiring Done entries](agent-data/notes.md#retiring-done-entries). Adopted and rejected retire
  the same way.

## custom.md: the project layer

[custom.md](custom.md) is an agent-file like the others, and the aim is that it stays as generic
as they do. Only what cannot be family-wide belongs here:

- **medium-determined**: the medium and its validation commands (what the per-commit checklist's
  "validate the artifact" runs), and versioning specifics beyond
  [versioning.md](notes/versioning.md). Not a divergence and not negotiable, since another
  medium could not adopt them if it wanted to.
- **elective divergence**: somewhere this project deliberately differs. An entry must say **why
  it cannot be family-wide**; with no answer it is an experiment and belongs in the pinned file
  where the rule lives (see [Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)).
- **the dogfood log**: dated entries on what this project is trying and where the instructions
  chafed, each carrying a status. In-flight entries only; resolved ones retire.

Precedence: custom.md is loaded last and wins conflicts with this file and the satellites.

old = ("Universal file, pinned to the template repository; do not edit here. Project overrides go in\n"

## docs: experiment in the local agent-files

- [[N]] 0.24.1 docs: experiment in the local agent-files

A single-commit cycle inverting hard rule 12: a proposed change to the agent-files (`AGENTS.md`,
`custom.md`, `agent-data/*`) is now edited into the member's local copy rather than staged as a
`custom.md` override or written into the template's shared payload. Raised by wink 2026-08-05
during the convergence discussion with vc-x1, and proposed to the family from here rather than as
a template edit, which is the new rule demonstrating itself.

The old rule had two costs, both structural:

- **`custom.md` was the staging area**, so every proposal landed there as an override. That
  guaranteed it accreted and drifted non-generic, against the goal of a `custom.md` that is
  generic at birth. Three of ours (write-to-full-width, cycle bookend titles, scope-based version
  advancement) were proposals wearing override clothing, and the 20260802 snapshot has since
  adopted all three family-wide
- **the shared payload was the only place to propose**, which makes it the one mutable resource
  two members can collide on. Mailboxes are per-member and do not serialize a payload write. This
  was found while drafting a reply to vc-x1: a two-tier "corrections go straight to the payload"
  scheme solved the ceremony and left the race

What replaces them, and why each record exists:

- **the diff** between a member and the payload is the live proposal set. It needs no maintenance
  and cannot go stale, which a hand-kept status list would
- **the commit history** is the durable record, and it matters because the diff is ephemeral by
  construction: at convergence the diff empties and every trace of what was proposed goes with
  it. History keeps the date, the author, the rationale, and via the `ochid:` trailer the
  bot-repo session that reasoned it out. That is why an agent-file change wants its own commit:
  ridden along inside a feature commit, the rule change survives as one file-by-file bullet
- **the dogfood log** carries what neither can derive, the why and the status, and it is now
  in-flight entries only

`custom.md` narrows to what cannot be family-wide, and the two kinds are worth separating because
only one is negotiable:

- **medium-determined** content (our `cargo fmt` / `clippy` / `cargo test` / `cargo doc`
  validation commands) is not a divergence at all. A prose repo could not adopt them if it wanted
  to, so there is nothing to converge on and no pushback is possible
- **elective divergence** is where wink's pushback belongs, and the test is structural rather
  than dependent on anyone noticing: an entry must say why it cannot be family-wide. With no
  answer it is an experiment, and it belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives

The cost, recorded rather than argued away: a local agent-file no longer distinguishes agreed
from proposed by reading it, which the pinned/`custom.md` split used to do structurally. Our own
2026-08-04 entry logged the same failure shape for doc links, that an unchecked surface reads as
authority until someone follows it. We think the fix is an acquaint-time diff against the payload,
one command reporting how far this member has drifted, which pairs with the `vc-x1 mailbox`
command proposed in the `[messages]` thread. Neither is built, so the exposure stands until they
are.

Not in scope here: reclassifying our existing `custom.md` entries against the new contract. Three
of them are already adopted family-wide, so they should be deleted rather than moved, and that
depends on the 20260803 baseline sync landing first. Carried as a `## Todo`.

  and cannot go stale, which a hand-kept status list would

  construction: at convergence the diff empties and every trace of what was proposed goes with
  it. History keeps the date, the author, the rationale, and via the `ochid:` trailer the
  bot-repo session that reasoned it out. That is why an agent-file change wants its own commit:
  ridden along inside a feature commit, the rule change survives as one file-by-file bullet

  in-flight entries only

  validation commands) is not a divergence at all. A prose repo could not adopt them if it wanted
  to, so there is nothing to converge on and no pushback is possible
- **elective divergence** is where wink's pushback belongs, and the test is structural rather
  than dependent on anyone noticing: an entry must say why it cannot be family-wide. With no
  answer it is an experiment, and it belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives

of them are already adopted family-wide, so they should be deleted rather than moved, and that

## 2026-08-05 from iiac-perf (o5) + wink: experiment in the local agent-files

A proposal for the family, landed here as `0.24.1` on bookmark `agent-files-model`. It inverts
hard rule 12. Rationale and the full argument are in
[chores-06](https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf/blob/main/notes/chores/chores-06.md#docs-experiment-in-the-local-agent-files);
this is the summary and the ask.

**Read the bootstrap first, so the diff does not look like us going off-protocol.** We proposed
this by editing our own local `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/*`, which is exactly what the proposal
asks the family to permit. That is deliberate: the first instance is the rule demonstrating
itself. If the family rejects it, the change retires the same way an adopted one would.

**The rule.** The agent-files are `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*`. The template's
payload is the read-only copy; a proposed change is edited into the member's local copy of the
file the rule lives in.

- the **diff** between a member and the payload is that member's live proposal set. No
  maintenance, cannot go stale
- the **commit history** is the durable record, and it matters because the diff is ephemeral: at
  convergence the diff empties and every trace of what was proposed goes with it. History keeps
  the date, the rationale, and via `ochid:` the session that reasoned it out. So an agent-file
  change is its own commit
- the **dogfood log** carries what neither derives, the why and a status, and is in-flight only.
  Resolved entries retire to `done.md` with the narrative in chores, adopted and rejected alike

**Two problems it fixes, both of which this week produced.**

- `custom.md` was the staging area for every proposal, so it accreted and drifted non-generic
  against the goal of a generic `custom.md`. Three of ours were proposals wearing override
  clothing, and your 20260802 snapshot has since adopted all three
- the shared payload was the only place to propose, making it the one resource two members can
  collide on. We found this drafting our reply to you: a two-tier "corrections go straight to the
  payload" scheme solved the ceremony and left the race untouched. Mailboxes are per-member and
  do not serialize a payload write

**`custom.md` narrows** to what cannot be family-wide, in two kinds, because only one is
negotiable: medium-determined content (our `cargo` validation commands, which a prose repo could
not adopt if it wanted to, so there is nothing to converge on), and elective divergence, where an
entry must say why it cannot be family-wide. With no answer it is an experiment and belongs in
the pinned file where the rule lives.

**The cost, stated rather than argued away.** A local agent-file no longer reads as
family-agreed, which the pinned / `custom.md` split used to guarantee structurally. Our own
2026-08-04 entry logged this failure shape for doc links: an unchecked surface reads as authority
until someone follows it. We think the fix is an acquaint-time diff against the payload, one
command reporting how far a member has drifted, pairing naturally with the `vc-x1 mailbox`
command from the `[messages]` thread. Neither is built, so the exposure stands.

**Files touched here**, as the shape of what the family would adopt: `AGENTS.md` hard rule 12 and
a new "Changing the agent-files" section, the `custom.md` contract section, the "do not edit
here" line in all five `agent-data/*` (it is the same line in each), and
`agent-data/notes.md`'s retire path gaining the agent-file case.

Done when: the family accepts, amends, or rejects. On acceptance the wording folds into the
payload and every member re-syncs; on rejection we retire it here and the history keeps the
reasoning. Either way it wants deciding before our baseline sync, since the sync would otherwise
overwrite it.

The two subsections below are the same session's family-convergence work. They are not about this
commit's change, but they are the durable home for findings that would otherwise live only in a
mailbox message, and the mailbox protocol is handle-then-delete.

### jj revset primer audit (2026-08-05)

The 20260803 baseline carries a Revsets primer in `agent-data/jj.md` that this repo has never
reviewed: 36 lines present in the payload and absent here, since our `jj.md` is the older subset.
A superset adopted sight-unseen is how a bad rule gets pinned family-wide, and one of these is
provably that. Audited against a live repo (132 visible commits, `main` at `pqxtvkmn`, two parked
bookmarks).

Verified and correct:

- revision forms, and ambiguous prefixes rejected rather than guessed: `jj log -r kv` gives
  "Error: Change ID prefix `kv` is ambiguous"
- neighbours `@-` parent, `@--` grandparent, `@+` child
- "a step past the end of the chain is the empty set, not an error": `@+` and `root()-` both
  return empty and exit cleanly
- `all()` is all visible commits, and the arithmetic closes: `all() ~ ::main` is 6, exactly what
  `main..` returns

**The error is the framing bullet, not the gloss beneath it.** The payload's `jj.md:41-42` reads
"Ranges pair a dot form with a direction, and `::` includes the implicit endpoint while `..`
excludes it", and `:43` then reads "`X::` descendants of X including X; `X..` descendants
excluding X". `X..` is not descendants of X. These are two different operators, not one with an
endpoint toggle:

- `A::B` is the DAG range: commits that are both descendants of A and ancestors of B
- `A..B` is the difference `::B ~ ::A`: ancestors of B that are not ancestors of A

The framing accidentally survives the `::X` / `..X` pair, where the only difference really is the
root commit, then fails completely on `X::` / `X..`. So correcting `:43` alone leaves the model
that generated it in place, and the next person to extend the primer reproduces the bug.

Measured here:

```
main..                    6 changes
descendants(main) ~ main  4 changes
~::main                   6 changes   (identical to main..)
::main                  126 changes   (includes main and the root commit)
..main                  125 changes   (same, root removed; main still included)
```

The two extra changes in `main..` are parked bookmarks, one of them `web-claude-tweaks`, which
`TODO.md` carries a standing entry to rebase. An agent following the gloss and running
`jj abandon 'main..'` would destroy work we have written down a plan to keep. Not a near miss: a
different set.

A second, quieter defect in the same block: `::X` and `..X` are both glossed as "ancestors of X"
and both **include X itself**, directly under a bullet that says "including X" explicitly for
`::`. A reader reasonably infers that `::X` excludes X. The "useful sets" bullet inherits it,
since `jj log -r ::@` is glossed "all ancestors of `@`" and is 130 of our 132 commits, `@`
included.

Proposed replacement for the two range bullets:

```
- Two range operators, not one with a toggle:
  - `A::B` is the DAG range: commits that are both descendants of A and ancestors of B,
    both ends included.
  - `A..B` is the difference `::B ~ ::A`: ancestors of B that are not ancestors of A.
- Omitting an operand defaults it, and that is where the two diverge sharply:
  - `X::` is `X::visible_heads()`: descendants of X, X included.
  - `X..` is `X..visible_heads()`, which is `~::X`: everything that is *not* an ancestor of
    X. This is not "descendants of X". On a repo with parked branches it pulls them in too.
    Descendants of X excluding X is `X:: ~ X`.
  - `::X` is `root()::X`: ancestors of X, with both X and the root commit included.
  - `..X` is `root()..X`: the same set with the root commit removed. X is still included.
```

One finding that is forward-looking rather than wrong today: the primer says `jj-tips.md` is
"hosted once in the template repository (custom.md records the template's path)". The file exists
at `vc-x1-template/jj-tips.md`, but our `custom.md` records no such path by name. Its only
`../vc-x1-template/...` strings are the two mailbox lines, and those are exactly what the proposed
`[messages]` move into `.vc-config.toml` deletes. The pointer dangles the moment that lands, and
should name the config key instead.

### Convergence measurements and positions (2026-08-05)

Measured independently rather than taken on report, `iiac-perf` against `vc-x1-template/work/`:

- diff line counts, ours-only / payload-only: `AGENTS.md` 15 / 23, `agent-data/code.md` 0 / 0
  (already byte-identical), `notes.md` 3 / 3, `prose.md` 8 / 19, `jj.md` 1 / 36
- `diff -r` of vc-x1's `AGENTS.md` plus `agent-data/` against the payload exits 0, so the payload
  and vc-x1 are byte-identical and convergence is one-directional: us adopting the baseline, not
  a three-way negotiation
- our `agent-data/` has `cycle.md` where the payload has `cycle-checklists.md`, and lacks
  `cycle-protocol.md` and `versioning.md`, which the payload relocated out of `notes/`
- our `cycle.md` has validation at step 4 and is self-consistent; the payload's own
  `work/custom.md:11` still cites step 4 against a checklist that renumbered validation to 5, so
  the payload is the inconsistent side

Sizing the sync from here: 6 mentions of `agent-data/cycle.md` in 1 file, 18 of
`notes/cycle-protocol.md` across 7, 4 of `notes/versioning.md` across 3. 28 inbound references to
re-point, which is why it is a cycle and not a side edit.

Positions taken on the four questions the family left open, recorded so they survive the mailbox:

- **how a pinned change is proposed**: split by kind. A correction (factual error, typo, stale
  cross-reference) goes straight into the payload, since a wrong gloss has no second opinion to
  gather; a rule change goes through a snapshot directory, reviewed as a set. This commit's own
  change supersedes the question for experiments, which now never touch the payload at all
- **the `jj.md` correction lands before our baseline sync**, not with it, and it must cover the
  framing bullet and not only the gloss, since syncing propagates the model
- **the CLI reads `[messages]`**: if it does not, unknown-key tolerance still has to be decided,
  so reading them answers the question instead of dodging it. One schema note: `other-repo`
  already sits under `[workspace]`, and if `community` is the same species it belongs in the same
  table
- **what a version bump promises**: `versioning.md` defines the scheme, each project's
  `custom.md` states the promise. The promise differs by artifact kind (binary crate, library
  crate, CLI with users, prose repo) and no shared file can assert one for everybody. Related and
  worth a rule of its own: a pinned file names no project, no project's history, and no project's
  versions

## 2026-08-05 from iiac-perf (o5) + wink: experiment in the local agent-files

A proposal for the family, landed here as `0.24.1`. It inverts hard rule 12. The full argument is
in
[chores-06](https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf/blob/main/notes/chores/chores-06.md#docs-experiment-in-the-local-agent-files);
this is the summary and the ask.

**Read the bootstrap first, so our diff does not look like us going off-protocol.** We proposed
this by editing our own local `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/*`, which is precisely what the proposal
asks the family to permit. The first instance is the rule demonstrating itself. If the family
rejects it, the change retires here the same way an adopted one would.

**The rule.** The agent-files are `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*`. The template's
payload is the read-only copy; a proposed change is edited into the member's local copy of the
file the rule lives in.

- the **diff** between a member and the payload is that member's live proposal set: no
  maintenance, cannot go stale
- the **history** is the durable record, and it matters because the diff is ephemeral. At
  convergence the diff empties and every trace of what was proposed goes with it. History keeps
  the date, the rationale, and via `ochid:` the session that reasoned it out. So an agent-file
  change is its own commit
- the **dogfood log** carries what neither derives, the why and a status, in-flight only. Resolved
  entries retire to `done.md` with the narrative in chores, adopted and rejected alike

**Two problems it fixes, both of which this week produced.** `custom.md` was the staging area for
every proposal, so it accreted against the goal of a generic `custom.md`; three of ours were
proposals wearing override clothing, and your 20260802 snapshot has since adopted all three. And
the shared payload was the only place to propose, making it the one resource two members can
collide on. We found that drafting our reply to you: a two-tier "corrections go straight to the
payload" scheme solved the ceremony and left the race untouched.

**`custom.md` narrows** to what cannot be family-wide, in two kinds, because only one is
negotiable. Medium-determined content (our `cargo` validation commands, which a prose repo could
not adopt if it wanted to) is not a divergence at all. Elective divergence is, and an entry must
say why it cannot be family-wide; with no answer it is an experiment and belongs in the pinned
file where the rule lives.

**The cost, stated rather than argued away.** A local agent-file no longer reads as
family-agreed, which the pinned / `custom.md` split used to guarantee structurally. Our own
2026-08-04 entry logged this exact shape for doc links: an unchecked surface reads as authority
until someone follows it. We think the fix is an acquaint-time diff against the payload, one
command reporting how far a member has drifted, pairing with the `vc-x1 mailbox` command from the
`[messages]` thread. Neither is built, so the exposure stands.

**Files touched**, as the shape of what the family would adopt: `AGENTS.md` hard rule 12 plus a
new "Changing the agent-files" section and the `custom.md` contract section; the "do not edit
here" line in all five `agent-data/*`, identical in each; and `agent-data/notes.md`'s retire path
gaining the agent-file case.

**We are dogfooding before asking you to decide**: the next cycle here runs under these rules from
a cold session, so the reply will carry evidence rather than only argument. Expect a follow-up.

Done when: the family accepts, amends, or rejects. On acceptance the wording folds into the
payload and every member re-syncs; on rejection we retire it here and the history keeps the
reasoning. Either way it wants deciding before our baseline sync, which would otherwise overwrite
it.
